findings.title: First offline access tokens are labeled as online sessions
findings.body: Access-token ids are encoded inside createClientAccessToken/initToken, which createTokenResponse calls on line 110 while userSession is still the online session, so the jti prefix is "on". Only after that does generateRefreshToken() create the offline user session (Keycloak keeps the same session id) and, when AuthenticationProcessor.FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS is set, line 120 deletes the online session — before the token is signed in build() and returned. By the time the client uses the access token, that session id exists only in the offline store, but the prefix says online. ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType has the same ordering: generateAccessToken() at line 139 runs before line 145 removes the online session whenever the refresh token is offline (not only the first issuance). This prefix is meant to skip the online-then-offline session lookup. Trusting "on" for these tokens misses the session and rejects valid access tokens from offline login. Resolve the final session store before encoding the id (or rewrite the id before signing).

findings.title: Access-token id matcher uses the wrong slice and inverted logic
findings.body: isAccessTokenId is supposed to require the new jti to embed the expected grant shortcut, but it does not. The wire format is six characters SSTTGG before the colon, so the grant shortcut is substring(4, 6). The matcher uses substring(3, 5) (last char of the token-type shortcut plus the first char of the grant; for onrtac:... that is "ta", not "ac") and returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut, so a real match would be rejected. For every built-in shortcut the wrong slice never equals the expected value (onrtrt yields "tr", not refresh shortcut "rt"), so the check is dead code: any prefix:uuid passes expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken even if the grant shortcut is wrong. A prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the assertion. Require a 6-character prefix and accept only when substring(4, 6) equals the expected shortcut.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor intends to reject a null raw token id, but the fourth Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType again (already checked on the previous line) and the message falsely says rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is stored. encodeTokenId concatenates it, and Java turns null into the literal "null", producing a jti such as onrtac:null. Every token built with a null raw id shares that jti, so revocation/replay checks keyed by token id cannot tell them apart. Require rawTokenId to be non-null.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing grant factories
findings.body: getShortcut() was added to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI with no default method. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it on every grant factory. A custom grant-type provider compiled against the previous interface has no such method and throws AbstractMethodError during startup, which fails deployment when that provider is installed. The javadoc also says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but the encoder and decoder require exactly two characters; an implementation that follows the javadoc mints access-token ids the default decoder cannot parse. Add a default that returns a stable 2-character shortcut (or "na") and document the exact length.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not checked against the fixed 2-character format
findings.body: Encoded access-token ids are session(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2)+':'+rawId, and getTokenContextFromTokenId throws if the prefix length is not 6. postInit stores OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() with no check that it is non-null, exactly two characters, free of ':', and unique. A shortcut of any other length (including the 3-letter form described on getShortcut) is accepted, encodeTokenId embeds it, and decoding later throws IllegalArgumentException, so those tokens cannot be interpreted. A null shortcut NPEs in ConcurrentHashMap.put during postInit and aborts startup with an unclear error. The lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType (around line 112) and getGrantTypeByShortcut (around line 130) also overwrites an existing shortcut without re-running the duplicate size check, so a newly deployed grant can steal another grant's shortcut and make already-issued tokens decode as the wrong grant. Validate length, charset, and uniqueness both at startup and on the lazy path, and name the conflicting grant ids in the error.

findings.title: Public Context copy constructor was deleted
findings.body: The line that captures grantType from form params replaced the public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor instead of being added inside the primary constructor. That copy constructor is part of the grant SPI context type. Callers that clone a context with new OAuth2GrantType.Context(existing) no longer compile, including any in-repo use that this edit did not update. The deletion looks accidental. Restore the copy constructor and copy grantType as well; a clone that leaves grantType null causes access tokens to be encoded with grant shortcut "na" even when the original request had a grant. The new formParams.getFirst call also NPEs if formParams is null, which the previous constructor accepted.

findings.title: Legacy token exchange still encodes grant type as unknown
findings.body: The grant shortcut is taken from ClientSessionContext attribute Constants.GRANT_TYPE; if it was never set, the id is encoded with "na". Token exchange does not go through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, so each provider must set the attribute itself. Only StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient does so (line 237). TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory still enables the legacy TOKEN_EXCHANGE feature as well as the v2 features, and the legacy V1 token-exchange provider builds access tokens in its own exchangeClientToOIDCClient path, which this PR does not change. Those tokens get grant shortcut "na" and cannot be distinguished from tokens whose grant was never recorded, so the token-exchange use case this PR is for will not see them. Any other TokenExchangeProvider that overrides exchangeClientToOIDCClient and does not call this method has the same gap. Set the attribute on the shared issuance path, not only in the standard v2 provider.

findings.title: Bad token-id error claims the whole id must be length 6
findings.body: When the prefix before ':' is not 6 characters, getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException saying the token id has 'Expected length of 6.' The check is only on that prefix. A valid encoded id is 6 prefix characters, a colon, and a 36-character UUID (43 characters). The message points operators at a 6-character jti and does not say which part failed. State that the context prefix before ':' must be exactly 6 characters.
